title: An orbit of a cartesian descent groupoid is saturated
statement: Let $p:X\to Y$ be a morphism of schemes [def-pc-scheme], $V\to X$ a scheme over $X$, and $D$ a transport descent datum [def-pd-descent-datum]. Let $s:R\to V$ and $q:R\to X$ exhibit $R=V\times_Y X$ for $V\to Y$ the composite with $p$ [def-pc-fibre-product]. Write $t:R\to V$ for the morphism obtained by transporting the universal point $s$ from $s\circ(V\to X)$ to $q$. For every $v\in V$, put $O_v=t(s^{-1}(\{v\}))$. Then $s^{-1}(O_v)=t^{-1}(O_v)$. No flatness, finiteness, surjectivity, or closed-point hypothesis is required.

proof.text: Transport naturality identifies transport of a map into R with its composite with t. The transported point lies over q, so t composed with V to X equals q. This uses the shared transport_left_naturality theorem, imported from its own module.

For maps g1,g2:W to R with g1 t = g2 s, use the cartesian square to construct c:W to R with c s = g1 s and c q = g2 q. Apply transport naturality twice and the cocycle law to obtain c t = g2 t. Likewise lift (t,s followed by V to X) to an inverse map i:R to R; naturality and the cocycle followed by transport_self give i s = t and i t = s.

If s(r) is in the orbit of v, choose r0 with s(r0)=v and t(r0)=s(r). Lift (r0,r) to a point of the scheme pullback of t and s. Compose its arrows using c from the previous step: c(z) has source v and target t(r). Thus t(r) belongs to the orbit. Apply this implication to i(r) and use i s=t and i t=s for the converse.

theorem descent_orbit_saturated
    {X Y R : Scheme.{u}} {p : X ⟶ Y} {V : Over X}
    (D : Over.DescentDatum p V) (s : R ⟶ V.left) (q : R ⟶ X) (t : R ⟶ V.left)
    (hsq : IsPullback s q (V.hom ≫ p) p)
    (ht : (D.transport (s ≫ V.hom) q
      (by simpa only [Category.assoc] using hsq.w) (Over.homMk s)).left = t)
    (v : V.left) :
    s ⁻¹' (t '' (s ⁻¹' {v})) = t ⁻¹' (t '' (s ⁻¹' {v}))
